input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

Cluster administrators get per-project reporting of idle and stale resources directly in
the RHOAI web console: an idle-workbench report showing each workbench's last activity,
owner, and reserved resources, and a stale pipeline-run report showing completed runs
older than a configurable age together with their retained artifacts. Either report can
be exported as CSV so administrators can act on the data outside the console. The reports
are read-only — they give administrators the confidence to reclaim capacity manually;
automated reclamation and cost/chargeback calculations remain out of scope.

## Scope

- Idle-workbench report, shown per project: for each workbench, its last activity
  (sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking), its owner, and its reserved
  resources.
- Stale pipeline-run report, shown per project: completed pipeline runs older than a
  configurable age, with their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run
  completion metadata.
- An administrator-configurable age threshold for the stale pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report, covering the columns the report displays.
- Read-only reporting only: no reclamation or deletion actions are offered from the
  reports (automated reclamation and cost/chargeback are out of scope for the strategy).
- Validation of the two passive data sources as part of delivery: confirm that the
  notebook controller's activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines' run-completion metadata
  expose the fields the reports need, in a form the console can read.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench
  report, then each workbench is listed with its last activity, owner, and reserved
  resources, populated from the notebook controller's activity tracking.
- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs, when an administrator opens the
  stale pipeline-run report, then the runs older than the configured age are listed with
  their retained artifacts, populated from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Given an administrator changes the stale-run age threshold, then the stale pipeline-run
  report reflects the new threshold.
- Given either report is displayed, when the administrator exports it as CSV, then a CSV
  containing the report's displayed columns is produced.
- The reports are visible to administrators consistent with the console's existing
  project-scoped RBAC.
- Every report field is verified to populate from its stated source (notebook-controller
  activity tracking for the workbench report; Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for the
  pipeline-run report) against live cluster data.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved
  resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking — covered by this
  epic.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age
  with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata — covered by this
  epic.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of either report — bundled with the P1 report work
  because it extends the same report surfaces and the same data-access plumbing; a
  separate epic would double-touch the same UI and data-access code.

## Risks / Notes

- The strategy assumes the notebook controller's per-workbench last-activity data is
  readable by the console. The architecture context confirms the tracking exists, but the
  console consumes the Kubernetes API and its established component integrations; if the
  last-activity timestamp is not exposed in a console-readable form, follow-up work in the
  notebook controller (Notebooks component, Workbenches team) will be required and the
  decomposition should be revisited.
- The notebook controller and Kubeflow Pipelines are passive components in this strategy:
  they keep working as-is, and their continued provision of the report data is validated
  by this epic's acceptance criteria rather than by separate validation epics.

# Document the idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

New Red Hat documentation topics that explain the console's idle-workbench and stale
pipeline-run reports and walk administrators through safe manual reclamation steps based
on the report data. The documentation is authored once the reports are implemented, so it
describes the delivered behavior — fields, thresholds, export, and reclamation guidance —
rather than an intended design.

## Scope

Content outline (authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- Explaining the idle-workbench report: what last activity, owner, and reserved resources
  mean, where the data comes from, and how to read the report to spot idle workbenches.
- Explaining the stale pipeline-run report: the configurable age threshold, retained
  artifacts, the underlying run metadata, and how to interpret run age.
- How to export either report as CSV and use the exported data.
- Safe reclamation steps an administrator can take based on the reports (manual actions
  only — automated reclamation and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope for the
  strategy), including the cautions that make reclamation safe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics explaining both reports (fields, data sources, interpretation) and
  CSV export are authored and delivered through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Safe manual reclamation steps are documented, consistent with the strategy's
  out-of-scope boundary on automated reclamation and cost/chargeback.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports by the
  console engineering team, and any inaccuracies found in review are corrected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps — covered by
  this epic.
